ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure is an ethyl ester carbonyl fragment, with the structure of ethoxy connected to carbonyl C(=O)OEt, and the left side of the carbonyl is connected to a C=C enol system; the left-end carbon of the alkene is also connected to CH3 and OH. In the lower part of the figure is an aryl fragment marked Ar; the benzylic carbon forms C=[OH+] with protonated oxygen, and this carbon is also connected to H and aryl. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the atom connectivity in the image, the upper fragment is read as CH3CH2O-C(=O)-C=C(C)O, and the shown alkene geometry is encoded with slashes, giving CCOC(=O)/C=C(/C)O. The lower Ar is treated as phenyl, and the protonated hydroxyl/oxonium forms a double bond with the benzylic carbon, corresponding to [OH+]=Cc1ccccc1. After ignoring the curved arrows, there is no ordinary covalent bond between the two fragments, so a dot is used to connect the two SMILES fragments.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: 1) Read the top fragment as an ethyl ester conjugated to an enol: CH3CH2O-C(=O)-C=C(C)O, with the depicted alkene geometry encoded by / and /. 2) Read the bottom fragment as a benzyl-type aromatic species with a protonated hydroxyl/oxonium, corresponding to [OH+]=Cc1ccccc1. 3) Ignore all curved arrows because the prompt asks for the transition-state structure only. 4) Combine the two fragments as a disconnected SMILES string with a dot: CCOC(=O)/C=C(/C)O.[OH+]=Cc1ccccc1.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上方是一个乙酯羰基片段，结构为乙氧基连接到羰基 C(=O)OEt，羰基左侧连着一个 C=C 烯醇体系，烯烃左端碳还连有 CH3 和 OH。图中下方是一个带 Ar 标记的芳香基片段，苄位碳与质子化氧形成 C=[OH+]，该碳还连 H 和芳基。图中有多条弯箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。
推理：按图像中的原子连接关系，上方片段读作 CH3CH2O-C(=O)-C=C(C)O，并用斜杠编码所示烯烃几何，得到 CCOC(=O)/C=C(/C)O。下方 Ar 按苯基处理，质子化羟基/氧鎓与苄位碳成双键，对应 [OH+]=Cc1ccccc1。忽略弯箭头后两个片段之间没有普通共价键，因此用点号连接两个 SMILES 片段。
